correctness.rationale: For each finite path-box, Manhattan intersection geometry bounds any two distinct centers to at most two common open neighbors, ruling out shattered sets of size four. Pair shattering follows a necessary-and-sufficient private-neighbor test, counted by axis and diagonal displacements. Triple shattering forces three distinct coordinate axes, and its only remaining obstacles are three isolated singleton traces; all possible spare directions are counted by the number of interior coordinates, producing the exact cubic formula. An independently constructed direct trace checker exhaustively agrees for 21 boxes (support sizes 0-4), including all dimension-three boundary cases. Finite verification is not substituted for the complete proof.

value.rationale: The all-parameter path-box formulas quantify the entire shattered support complex, not merely the known universal dimension ceiling. Boundary effects cause an exact two-exception VC transition in dimension three and change the number of shattered triples even when the VC dimension is fixed. The derived low-degree support polynomials are natural structural invariants for local vertex-neighborhood learning and finite grid products, with immediate use in comparing different side lengths.
